speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Good evening everyone, hope you're well.  We'll take a show of hands, please.  
You've got one more year of your contract, but are  you able to give us an insight into the future and  
what your plans are? Congratulate Arsenal, Mikel,  staff, backroom staff, for this Premier League.  
Well deserved. At the same time, in my manager  career, one of the years that we fought more,  
with incredible things that we could not control.  And we were there. Never give up, give up. I would  
have loved to arrive in the last moment to try.  Of course, it was in their hands. But yeah, today  
the fatigue was there. So 12 days to prepare that  game. They played for the qualification for the  
Champions League. Extraordinary team, incredible,  well managed. And three days, three days, three  
days from Crystal Palace to today. The brilliance  of the players, we missed it. Our impact for  
the fresh players was not good enough, for the  players coming from the bench. We broke the team,  
the tempo that we had. We wanted to play a lot of  short passes. To make a lot of transitions against  
Bournemouth is so difficult. That's why Kova,  Rodri, Bernardo and the players inside to make  
short passes. I think we've been really good  for 90 minutes. We could not concede. We had  
our chance in the second half with Nico and  the linesman. How quick he made the action. So  
one against one from Erling should be good to see  onside or offside. And he didn't do it. But yeah,  
we fought incredibly a lot. And yeah, prepare  next season. Are you still going to be in charge?  
Listen, with the club, always I talk. But not now,  three or four seasons ago, when it was one year  
left. So when we extend or not, on that question,  first you have to understand I should talk with my  
chairman first, right? And after that, when I talk  with my chairman, we decide. I have one more year.  
We talk everything and we will decide. Do you know  when that's likely? No, no. We are talking in the  
next days. Yeah. Because always, I said always,  I said that when you are fighting for the titles,  
qualification for the Champions League, or Premier  League, or FA Cup, you don't decide for that  
reason. You don't go in the first moment there is  a problem, the players don't follow you anymore,  
and you have to stay there. And always we talk  with my chairman. When we talk, Pep, what are we  
going to do? When to do it? I said, let the season  go. When it will be over, we'll talk. But I think  
he deserves, right? And I deserve first to talk  with him, what we have to do. You've seemed very  
nostalgic over the last few months. You've seemed  quite emotional, talking about memories and the  
things you miss about football. Is that the kind  of headspace you've been in? Have you been making  
those decisions and having those thoughts?  No, it's been a tough year. It's been so,  
it's been a good year, honestly. It's been a  good year for many, many situations. It was tough  
playing against an excellent team, but absolutely  excellent team like Arsenal, the finalists for the  
Champions League. No, I'm fine. I'm fine. So now  is the moment with Ferran, especially my chairman,  
to talk and after that we'll see what happens.  You've obviously pushed Arsenal to the last week,  
won two trophies. It's still a very, very young  squad. Do you feel that whoever's in charge in the  
future, with or without you, is still that? I  had the feeling that the season always has to be,  
the perspective is good, you know, for many,  many years, experience for many, many leagues,  
pretending it's done. You have to win every  week and every game and every month. You have  
to win it again. There's nothing for granted. So  next season, we'll be back. The City will be back  
and we will try to bring the team in that sense,  competing until the end in the competitions. And  
sometimes you win. It happens. That's two times.  Sometimes you lose in the last moment because the  
opponents are really good, really tough, and this  is what we have to try again. Obviously, there's  
been a lot of new players over the last 18 months,  which you've discussed before. How pleased have  
you been over the last two months with the level  of performance and how they're sort of growing?  
Since January, it was really good. With a lot of  injuries and many, many things you don't control.  
I learned a lot this season. What do you have to  do to win? You have to make out of points. You  
have to win a good advantage, otherwise there  are circumstances that you cannot control. So  
we played in many, many moments with difficulties  and never give up, give up. And that's why we are  
here. I would love to arrive until the last moment  against Aston Villa at home with the chance,  
but unfortunately we did not win because today we  missed that pace, that situation that is required  
to play teams like Bournemouth. They are unbeaten  in 70 games and beaten and beaten, because they  
are really, really good side. And three days,  the travel to London. For example, Chelsea was  
not a brilliant, brilliant final. It's because you  need to be fresh in many things. And our calendar  
was really tough in the last part of the season.  You went to the City fans tonight. They obviously  
love you. They'll be going to the game on Sunday,  suddenly wondering if it is the last time. What  
do you say to those City fans tonight? Let me talk  about my chairman. So I know they love me so much.  
I love you more. So I know that. So it's the best  place to be. I love that place. So I adore it. So  
let me talk about my club, right? Even the people  say I talk 1,000 million people in person. And  
just I was incredibly, incredibly focused in  my job. And when we are in the competitions,  
I'm there. I was there. And this is  what I have to do then. Thank you guys.
title: Pep Guardiola post-match press conference | Bournemouth 1-1 Manchester City | Premier League
